title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an insider misuse case, not a model failure. A person with legitimate access to law enforcement systems is accused of querying them for a purpose unrelated to police work. The systems named, a camera network, a tag reader network and a state criminal justice database, were each built and authorised for investigative use, and the alleged misuse happened inside that authorised access rather than through any break in the technology.

The failure sits at the point of use, where access controls grant a query and nothing in the workflow requires the officer to record a case-linked reason that a second party reviews. Catching conduct of this kind depends on audit trails that log who searched for whom, and on someone comparing those logs against active cases. Whether such logging existed here, and whether anyone reviewed it during the period in question, is not established by the reporting.

The account rests on an indictment, which is an accusation and not a finding of guilt. Rozar has been released on bond and is scheduled for arraignment, and no verdict or admission is reported. The reporting does not establish his intent, nor does it establish what internal oversight, if any, was in place at the sheriff's office at the time.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, was released on bond after a grand jury indicted him on eight counts, including stalking and misuse of law enforcement databases. The 49-year-old is accused of using the sheriff's office camera system, tag reader system, and the Georgia Crime Information Center database for personal reasons between April and May 2024. He was terminated when the investigation began and was arrested on May 5.

The woman he allegedly tracked spoke anonymously, saying she hopes her story encourages other women to report abuse. The Georgia Bureau of Investigation led the multi-year investigation, which former Sheriff Doyle Wooten requested in 2024. Rozar is scheduled for arraignment on May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
